 SARS tax deadline: What happens if you miss Friday’s cut-off? 
 Taxpayers who fail to submit outstanding income tax returns by the deadline could face recurring administrative penalties rather than a once-off fine.
 15 seconds ago 
 Nompilo Kunene
 3 minutes read

 South African taxpayers have until Friday, 23 October, to submit their 2026 individual income tax returns or correct their auto-assessments, with those who miss the deadline potentially facing monthly penalties.
 The South African Revenue Service (SARS) has warned taxpayers about the financial consequences of failing to meet their tax obligations, with penalties determined by taxable income and potentially reaching R16,000 a month for high-income earners.
 ALSO READ | SARS targets informal economy and taxi industry in tax crackdown 
 The deadline applies to individual taxpayers who are required to file returns, including those who received auto-assessments but identified errors or missing information that need to be corrected.
 What happens if you miss the deadline?
 Taxpayers who fail to submit outstanding income tax returns by the deadline could face recurring administrative penalties rather than a once-off fine.
 According to SARS, penalties are based on taxable income and can be imposed monthly until the outstanding return is submitted or the maximum penalty period is reached.
 The penalties can accumulate for up to 35 months where SARS has the taxpayer’s correct address, or up to 47 months where the address is outdated.
 ALSO READ | Here’s what to do after receiving your SARS auto-assessment 
 The monthly penalties vary according to income, with amounts ranging from R250 for taxpayers in the lowest penalty bracket to as much as R16,000 for high-income earners.
 Based on a 35-month penalty period, the cumulative amount could reach R8,750 for the lowest bracket, R17,500 for the R500 penalty bracket and up to R560,000 for those facing the maximum monthly penalty.
 Do you still need to file if you earn less than R500,000?
 Not every taxpayer is required to submit a return.
 SARS has indicated that certain individuals who earned R500,000 or less from a single employer during the 2026 tax year may be exempt from filing, provided they meet the applicable requirements.
 However, taxpayers should not assume they are exempt based on their salary alone.
 Other factors may affect whether a return is required, and tax experts advise individuals with an active income tax reference number to check their SARS profiles for outstanding returns.
 Where SARS records show that a return is outstanding, failure to submit it could result in administrative penalties.
 ALSO READ | Hawks arrest Durban businessman over alleged R36 million SARS cigarette fraud 
 Taxpayers should therefore confirm their filing obligations through SARS before deciding not to submit a return.
 Auto-assessments: Friday is also the deadline to make corrections
 Friday’s deadline also marks the end of the filing window for individual taxpayers who received auto-assessments but need to dispute or correct the information used by SARS.
 Auto-assessments were issued during the opening weeks of the tax season, with eligible taxpayers receiving refunds shortly after their assessments were finalised.
 However, taxpayers were required to review the information used in their assessments and ensure it accurately reflected their financial circumstances.
 Those who identified missing information or errors could make corrections, with some cases requiring a manual tax return.
 Taxpayers who flagged an issue but have not yet completed the required corrections should do so before Friday’s deadline.
 Can you get an extension if you miss Friday’s deadline?
 Missing the deadline does not necessarily mean taxpayers have no further options, but an extension is not automatic.
 Taxpayers may approach SARS to request an extension, providing valid reasons for failing to submit their returns on time. These could include illness, missing documentation, technical difficulties or other mitigating circumstances.
 ALSO READ | SARS tax season guide: Key filing dates, tips and deadlines 
 Any extension remains subject to SARS approval. Taxpayers should follow the official process and wait for confirmation of the outcome and any revised submission deadline.
 The safest option for those who are required to file is to submit their returns before Friday rather than rely on an extension being granted.
 Who still has until January to file?
 The 23 October deadline does not apply to every category of taxpayer.
 Provisional taxpayers and trusts have until 22 January 2027 to submit their returns.
 The 2026 tax season deadlines are:
 Individual taxpayers: 23 October 2026
 Provisional taxpayers: 22 January 2027
 Trusts: 22 January 2027
 Taxpayers who are unsure of their filing status or have outstanding returns should check their SARS profiles and confirm their obligations before the applicable deadline.
